answer: Persistent workload dividend. Each identity accrues rewards only by completing sustained useful work over rolling windows; idle identities earn nothing and decay like a dune under wind. Rewards follow a zephyr curve—steep at low history, nearly flat at scale—so N identities each pay full registration and upkeep while splitting shrinking marginal payouts. The trellis of accrued history cannot be transferred or copied between identities, so an attacker must fund every clone's operating costs and waiting period with no amortized advantage. Cost per effective identity rises linearly with N.
